classification.difficultyReason: Combine concurrence, elimination and equal gradients to determine two unknown coefficients.

content.prompt: The line $ax+by=6$ is concurrent with the lines $4x-3y=17$ and $4x+y=-19$ and is parallel to the line $y=6x$. Find the values of $a$ and $b$.

answer.short:
$a=-6$, $b=1$.

Find the common point of the two given lines, then use equal gradients and substitute that point into $ax+by=6$.
answer.worked:
Subtract the second given equation from the first:
$$\begin{align*}(4x-3y)-(4x+y)&=17-(-19)\\-4y&=36\\y&=-9.
\end{align*}$$
Substitute into $4x+y=-19$:
$$\begin{align*}4x-9&=-19\\4x&=-10\\x&=-\frac52.
\end{align*}$$
Thus the common point is $\left(-\frac52,-9\right)$. Since $ax+by=6$ is parallel to $y=6x$, its gradient is $6$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-\frac abx+\frac6b\\-\frac ab&=6\\a&=-6b.
\end{align*}$$
Substitute the common point and $a=-6b$ into $ax+by=6$:
$$\begin{align*}-\frac52a-9b&=6\\-\frac52(-6b)-9b&=6\\6b&=6\\b&=1\\a&=-6.
\end{align*}$$
Check: $-6\left(-\frac52\right)+(-9)=6$, and $-6x+y=6$ rearranges to $y=6x+6$, which has gradient $6$.
